want.who_she_is: Josie Marsh, 18. Two suitcases in a room that was an office until Sunday. Her mother Dee married Ray Kessler in June and the house came with him, and with his son Wes, 20, a junior at the college she starts tomorrow. She has been in this house four hours. What she has to lose: nobody in it has a read on her yet — that is the only thing she owns, and every rung spends some of it.
want.obligation: The dues — Friday, at the pledge house, Simone counts them on the office desk and writes a name down if the number is short. Tuition is Ray's; everything college charges ON TOP of tuition is hers. THE OFFER (R5e): Ray covers the dues, reachable while she is fine and NOT gated on being short — owing him opens his ladder. Campus charges her, the debt lands at home.
want.appetite: To be the one who gets asked — by the people who set the rules, in the rooms where the rules are set — and to hear her own name said in a room she has not walked into yet. Cannot complete: every room has a room behind it, and campus keeps supplying people who have not looked at her yet. Where the bill stops being the reason: the Friday she has the dues folded in her pocket, walks past the office desk, and asks Ray for it anyway.
want.ascent: Bottom: the lecture hall, the dining hall, the sign-in book at the pledge house, the upstairs bathroom at home when it is free. Top: up the stairs at the pledge house on a party night without being stopped; into Halloran's office after the department has emptied; into the kitchen at one in the morning when Ray is the only one awake and nobody is pretending it is about the dues.
